reading.body:
Meta's Los Lunas campus in Valencia County, New Mexico, does not publish its power capacity. The operator reports $2.5B+ in cumulative investment since groundbreaking in 2016, 400+ operational jobs at full scale, and peak construction of 1,100 skilled trade workers on site. The specific megawatt footprint of the campus itself remains undisclosed, making its scale relative to other AI infrastructure sites impossible to assess from published figures alone.

The campus achieves LEED Gold certification for buildings. Meta reports that electricity use is matched with 100 percent clean and renewable energy and that a Meta-supported project is adding 885 megawatts of new renewable energy and 100 megawatts of battery storage in New Mexico. No published capacity figures exist for any of the 14 mapped facilities in the state, so the contribution of Los Lunas to the state's published AI infrastructure baseline cannot be calculated.

This campus matters to AI infrastructure tracking primarily as a long-term capital commitment by a hyperscale operator in a state with significant renewable energy development underway. Without published power figures, it functions as a known dark node in the continental grid: confirmed built, confirmed operating at scale, confirmed tied to renewable procurement in the region, and wholly absent from any public capacity accounting.
